title: in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, "Defect heuristic 2" treats an EMPTY ARRAY as a healthy val
description:
in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, "Defect heuristic 2" treats an EMPTY ARRAY as a healthy value, so a gap whose defect is an empty result verifies as FIXED while the defect is present. Verified live: resolving {"type":"fossilRankReport"} returns {"fossils":[],"ceiling":2000} while two source files sit over the ceiling of 2000 lines (3133 and 2780). A predicate using nonzero_field: "fossils" therefore returns 'absent' — defect fixed — on that empty array.

This is a ONE-LINE edit. Use the short anchor given; do not re-derive or paraphrase it.

The anchor string is:

val === 0 || val === null

It occurs exactly once in the file, on the line reading:

      if (val === 0 || val === null || val === undefined || val === '') {

Replace that entire line with:

      if (val === 0 || val === null || val === undefined || val === '' || (Array.isArray(val) && val.length === 0)) {

That is the only change. Do not modify the enclosing `if (nonzeroField !== null) {` block, the `return 'present';` inside it, the `return 'absent';` after it, or defect heuristics 1, 3 and 4.

Why this is correct: `nonzero_field` promises "this field should be non-zero, and a zero value means the defect is still present". An empty array is the array spelling of zero — a detector that returned no findings found nothing, which is exactly the defect state such a gap describes. Every existing case (0, null, undefined, "") keeps its current verdict, and any non-empty array or non-zero scalar still returns 'absent' exactly as before, so no currently-passing behaviour changes.

The file must typecheck. The vessel has a standing baseline of pre-existing test failures unrelated to this change; compare newly-failing tests rather than absolute counts.
